name: Lord Rama
description: Seventh avatar of Vishnu. Prince of Ayodhya, embodiment of dharma, the ideal man (Maryada Purushottam).

name: Mother Sita
description: Daughter of the Earth, princess of Mithila, wife of Rama. Embodiment of purity, devotion, and inner strength.

name: Bharata
description: Rama's devoted half-brother who refused the throne and ruled as regent placing Rama's sandals (paduka) on the throne.

name: Hanuman
description: Son of Vayu and Anjana, greatest devotee of Rama, who leapt across the ocean and burned Lanka.

name: Lakshmana
description: Rama's devoted younger brother, son of Sumitra, who followed him into exile. An avatar of Shesha Naga.

name: Shatrughna
description: Youngest son of Dasharatha, twin to Lakshmana, son of Sumitra. Slayer of Lavanasura in the Uttara Kanda.

name: Dasharatha
description: King of Ayodhya and father of Rama. A great warrior bound by his word, who died grief-stricken at Rama's exile.

name: Janaka (Seeradhwaja)
description: Philosopher-king of Mithila, foster-father of Sita whom he found in a furrow. A rajarshi (royal sage).

name: Kaikeyi
description: Second queen of Dasharatha, mother of Bharata. Her two boons, influenced by Manthara, sent Rama into exile.

name: Kausalya
description: Chief queen of Dasharatha and mother of Rama. A woman of dignity and unwavering dharma.

name: Sumitra
description: Third queen of Dasharatha, mother of Lakshmana and Shatrughna. Known for her wisdom and balanced counsel.

name: Sunayana
description: Queen of Janaka and foster-mother of Sita.

name: Agastya
description: Great southern sage who gave Rama the bow of Vishnu, the quiver of Brahma, and the Aditya Hridaya mantra.

name: Ahalya
description: Wife of sage Gautama, turned to stone by his curse and redeemed by the dust of Rama's feet.

name: Anasuya
description: Wife of Atri, model of wifely devotion, who gave Sita celestial garments and ornaments.

name: Atri
description: One of the Saptarishis whose ashram Rama, Sita and Lakshmana visited at the start of their exile.

name: Bharadwaja
description: Great sage of Prayag at the confluence of Ganga and Yamuna who welcomed Rama and Sita during exile.

name: Gautama Maharshi
description: Husband of Ahalya and father of Shatananda. A stern ascetic of Mithila.

name: Narada
description: Devarshi who narrated the essence of Rama's life to Valmiki, sparking the composition of the Ramayana.

name: Valmiki
description: Adi Kavi, the first poet, composer of the Ramayana. Former hunter Ratnakara, transformed by the name of Rama.

name: Vasishta
description: Kulaguru (family preceptor) of the Ikshvakus, one of the seven great rishis, keeper of Kamadhenu.

name: Vishwamitra
description: Once a mighty king, who by fierce tapas became a Brahmarshi. Took Rama and Lakshmana to protect his yagna.

name: Aditi
description: Mother of the Adityas and the devas, invoked in the Ikshvaku genealogies.

name: Agni
description: Fire god and father of Nila; witness to Sita's Agni-pariksha after the war.

name: Ashwini Kumaras
description: Twin physicians of the devas and fathers of the vanara brothers Mainda and Dvivida.

name: Bhudevi (Earth)
description: The Earth goddess, true mother of Sita, who at last opens her arms to receive her daughter back.

name: Brahma
description: The four-faced creator of the worlds, whose boons to Ravana and blessings to Rama shape the story.

name: Chandra
description: The Moon god, referenced in similes and invocations throughout the Ramayana.

name: Ganga
description: River goddess brought to earth by Bhagiratha; Rama crosses her with Guha's help at Shringverapura.

name: Garuda
description: King of birds and mount of Vishnu, who freed Rama and Lakshmana from Indrajit's naga-noose.

name: Indra
description: King of the devas, father of Vali and adversary of Ravana and Meghanada (Indrajit).

name: Kamadeva
description: God of desire whose burning by Shiva in Dandaka gives the Dandakaranya its lore.

name: Kamadhenu (Shabala)
description: Divine cow of plenty kept by Vasishta, whose capture by Vishwamitra's forces began his long tapas.

name: Kashyapa Prajapati
description: Prajapati sage-god, father of devas and asuras; ancestor in the cosmic genealogy.

name: Kubera
description: Lord of wealth and half-brother of Ravana who originally ruled Lanka before being driven out.

name: Lakshmi
description: Consort of Vishnu; Sita is her descent into human form for the sake of Rama.

name: Nandi
description: Gana of Shiva whose curse on Ravana foretold his destruction at the hands of a monkey-aided prince.

name: Parashurama
description: Sixth avatar of Vishnu, the axe-wielding Bhargava, who challenged Rama after the breaking of Shiva's bow.

name: Parvati
description: Consort of Shiva, present in the cosmic background of the epic and in dialogue frames of later tradition.

name: Rati
description: Consort of Kamadeva, goddess of love.

name: Sachi
description: Consort of Indra, whose modesty is contrasted with the wild force of the rakshasis.

name: Saraswati
description: Goddess of speech and learning; the river invoked in the opening of the epic.

name: Shesha (Ananta)
description: Thousand-headed cosmic serpent on whom Vishnu reclines; incarnates as Lakshmana to serve Rama.

name: Shiva
description: The Destroyer, whose great bow Rama broke at Sita's swayamvara and whose grace is central to the epic.

name: Surasa
description: Mother of the nagas, who tested Hanuman mid-ocean by demanding to swallow him before letting him pass.

name: Surya
description: The Sun god, father of Sugriva and ancestor of the Ikshvaku (Solar) line; giver of the Aditya Hridaya to Rama.

name: Varuna
description: God of the ocean who appeared before Rama and showed him the way across the sea to Lanka.

name: Vayu
description: Wind god and true father of Hanuman, who carries the Sanjivani mountain through the skies of the war.

name: Vishnu
description: The Preserver, who descends as Rama for the slaying of Ravana at the prayer of the devas.

name: Vishwakarma
description: Celestial architect, father of Nala, builder of Lanka and of the celestial weapons.

name: Yama
description: God of death and dharma who once fled before Ravana and whom Rama consulted in the Uttara Kanda.

name: Angiras
description: One of the Saptarishis, a progenitor of the Angirasa Brahmin lineage.

name: Bhrigu
description: One of the Saptarishis, progenitor of the Bhargava lineage that includes Parashurama.

name: Chyavana
description: Bhargava sage famed for his tapas, mentioned in the Ikshvaku legends.

name: Durvasa
description: Quick-tempered sage whose visit to Rama's court set in motion the departure of Lakshmana.

name: Jabali
description: Minister-sage of Dasharatha who argued with Rama in Chitrakoot from a materialist viewpoint, to test him.

name: Jamadagni
description: Father of Parashurama, a great Bhargava sage of the solar lineage.

name: Kashyapa
description: Prajapati sage, father of devas, daityas, and most beings, included among Dasharatha's ritvijas.

name: Kratu
description: One of the seven mind-born sons of Brahma and a Saptarishi.

name: Lopamudra
description: Wife of sage Agastya, herself a learned rishika who composed hymns of the Rig Veda.

name: Mandakarni
description: Ascetic of Panchavati region who stood in water for years; the devas sent apsaras to disturb his tapas.

name: Marichi
description: Mind-born son of Brahma, father of Kashyapa. Not to be confused with the rakshasa Maricha.

name: Markandeya
description: Long-lived sage and member of Dasharatha's council.

name: Matanga
description: Sage of the Rishyamuka region whose ashram became Shabari's home after his ascent.

name: Pulaha
description: One of the seven mind-born sons of Brahma.

name: Pulastya
description: One of the seven mind-born sons of Brahma and grandfather of Ravana, Kubera, Kumbhakarna and Vibhishana.

name: Renuka
description: Wife of Jamadagni and mother of Parashurama.

name: Rishyasringa
description: Young sage whose arrival ended a drought in Anga. Performed Dasharatha's Putrakameshti yagna that led to Rama's birth.

name: Saubhari
description: Ancient sage referenced in the Ikshvaku legends recited to Rama.

name: Shabari
description: Tribal devotee of Rama who tasted each fruit to ensure none was sour before offering it to him.

name: Sharabhanga
description: Ascetic whom Rama met in the Dandaka forest, who ascended to Brahmaloka after beholding Rama.

name: Shatananda
description: Chief priest of Janaka, eldest son of the sage Gautama and Ahalya.

name: Sutikshna
description: Disciple of Agastya who hosted Rama in his ashram and directed him onward to Agastya.

name: Suyajna
description: Son of Vasishta, priest of Ayodhya invoked during Dasharatha's sacrifices.

name: Svayamprabha
description: Tapasvini in the magical cave (Rikshabila) who sheltered Hanuman's search party and led them to the sea.

name: Trinabindu
description: Sage whose curse features in the Pulastya-Kaikasi ancestry of the rakshasas.

name: Vamadeva
description: Ancient rishi and member of Dasharatha's council of priests.

name: Vibhandaka
description: Father of Rishyasringa, a stern forest sage who had raised his son in complete ignorance of women.

name: Vishrava
description: Son of Pulastya, father of Kubera (by Ilavida) and of Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Vibhishana and Shurpanakha (by Kaikasi).

name: Angada (son of Vali)
description: Crown prince of Kishkindha, son of Vali and Tara. Led the southern search for Sita and served as Rama's envoy to Ravana.

name: Guha
description: Chief of the Nishadas at Shringverapura who ferried Rama across the Ganga and loved him as a brother.

name: Jambavan
description: Ancient bear king (Rikshraj), elder among Sugriva's counsellors, who reminded Hanuman of his own strength.

name: Jatayu
description: Eagle king and friend of Dasharatha who battled Ravana to rescue Sita and died in Rama's arms.

name: Nala
description: Son of Vishwakarma, the vanara architect who engineered the bridge (Setu) across the ocean to Lanka.

name: Nila
description: Son of Agni, commander-in-chief of Sugriva's army, a fierce warrior of the siege of Lanka.

name: Sampati
description: Elder brother of Jatayu, the aged eagle who told the vanaras that Sita was held in Lanka.

name: Sugriva
description: Son of Surya, king of the Vanaras of Kishkindha after the death of his brother Vali, and steadfast ally of Rama.

name: Tara
description: Wise queen of Vali, later of Sugriva. Her counsel saved Lakshmana's wrath and kept the vanara alliance together.

name: Vibhishana
description: Righteous brother of Ravana who chose dharma, joined Rama and was crowned king of Lanka after the war.

name: Aja
description: Son of Raghu and father of Dasharatha. Ruled Ayodhya with justice.

name: Ambarisha
description: Pious Ikshvaku king whose sacrifice features the tale of the boy Shunahshepa being rescued by Vishwamitra.

name: Amshuman
description: Grandson of Sagara who recovered the sacrificial horse and learned the fate of his ancestors from Garuda.

name: Anaranya
description: Ikshvaku king who fought Ravana and, in dying, prophesied Ravana's destruction at the hands of a descendant — Rama.

name: Angada (son of Lakshmana)
description: Son of Lakshmana and Urmila; made king of Karupada by Rama. Not to be confused with Vali's son.

name: Asamanjas
description: Sagara's wicked son, banished for tormenting the citizens of Ayodhya. Father of Amshuman.

name: Ashwapati
description: King of Kekaya, maternal grandfather of Bharata and father of Kaikeyi.

name: Bhagiratha
description: Great king whose tapas brought the Ganga down from heaven to liberate the sixty thousand sons of Sagara.

name: Chandraketu
description: Son of Lakshmana and Urmila, made king of Chandrakanta.

name: Dilipa
description: Son of Amshuman. Despite his tapas, failed to bring down the Ganga for the salvation of Sagara's sons.

name: Harishchandra
description: Son of Trishanku. Legendary for his unwavering truthfulness even when reduced to a cremation-ground keeper.

name: Ikshvaku
description: Founder of the Solar (Suryavamsha) dynasty, eldest son of Manu, after whom the Ikshvaku lineage is named.

name: Kakutstha (Puranjaya)
description: Ancestor of Rama who rode on the hump of Indra (in bull form) to defeat the asuras — source of the epithet 'Kakutstha'.

name: Kalmashapada
description: Ikshvaku king also known as Saudasa, cursed to become a rakshasa after offending Vasishta.

name: Kusha
description: Son of Rama and Sita, born in Valmiki's ashram. Inheritor of the southern Kosala kingdom.

name: Kushadhwaja
description: Younger brother of Janaka, king of Sankashya, father of Mandavi and Shrutakirti.

name: Lava
description: Son of Rama and Sita, twin to Kusha. Taught the Ramayana by Valmiki and sang it in Rama's court.

name: Mandavi
description: Daughter of Kushadhwaja (Janaka's brother), wife of Bharata.

name: Mandhata
description: Legendary Ikshvaku emperor whose empire extended to the ends of the earth.

name: Manthara
description: The hunchbacked maidservant of Kaikeyi whose poisoned counsel triggered Rama's exile.

name: Manu (Vaivasvata)
description: Progenitor of the Ikshvaku line and the present manvantara. Son of Surya, lawgiver of mankind.

name: Nimi
description: Son of Ikshvaku and founder of the Mithila (Videha) line. Cursed by Vasishta, he became the blinking of the eyes.

name: Pushkala
description: Son of Bharata and Mandavi. Founded the city of Pushkalavati.

name: Raghu
description: Illustrious ancestor of Rama, after whom the Raghuvamsha (Raghu dynasty) is named.

name: Romapada
description: King of Anga, foster-father of Shanta, who invited Rishyasringa to end a famine and performed his marriage.

name: Sagara
description: Ikshvaku emperor, father of sixty thousand sons who were burnt to ashes by Kapila's glance while searching for the sacrificial horse.

name: Shanta
description: Daughter of Dasharatha, given in adoption to King Romapada of Anga. Wife of the sage Rishyasringa.

name: Shatrughati
description: Son of Shatrughna, installed as king of Vidisha.

name: Shrutakirti
description: Daughter of Kushadhwaja, wife of Shatrughna.

name: Subahu (son of Shatrughna)
description: Son of Shatrughna, installed as king of Mathura after the death of Lavanasura.

name: Sumantra
description: Chief minister and charioteer of Dasharatha who drove Rama to the forest and returned heartbroken.

name: Taksha
description: Son of Bharata and Mandavi. Founded the city of Takshashila in the northwest.

name: Trishanku
description: Ikshvaku king who sought heaven in his mortal body. Suspended between earth and heaven by Vishwamitra as Trishanku's constellation.

name: Urmila
description: Daughter of Janaka, wife of Lakshmana. She accepted separation for fourteen years so Lakshmana could serve Rama.

name: Yudhajit
description: Brother of Kaikeyi, prince of Kekaya, who took Bharata and Shatrughna to his kingdom before Rama's exile.

name: Anjana
description: Apsara-born mother of Hanuman, wife of Kesari.

name: Dadhimukha
description: Maternal uncle of Sugriva and guardian of the sacred Madhuvana grove raided by the returning vanara host.

name: Dvivida
description: Vanara warrior, brother of Mainda, son of the Ashwini Kumaras.

name: Gaja
description: Vanara warrior chief in Sugriva's forces.

name: Gavaksha
description: Vanara commander of a large troop listed among Sugriva's ministers.

name: Gavaya
description: Vanara chief commanding a mighty division in Sugriva's army.

name: Kesari
description: Foster-father of Hanuman, a mighty vanara chief.

name: Kumuda
description: Vanara chief listed among Sugriva's warriors at Kishkindha.

name: Mainda
description: Vanara warrior, brother of Dvivida, son of the Ashwini Kumaras.

name: Panasa
description: Vanara commander of great strength listed in Sugriva's council.

name: Rishabha
description: Vanara commander listed among Sugriva's chiefs at the march on Lanka.

name: Ruma
description: Wife of Sugriva, taken by Vali during the brothers' estrangement and restored to Sugriva after Vali's fall.

name: Sharabha
description: Vanara chief commanding a division of Sugriva's host.

name: Shatabali
description: Vanara chief leading the search party of the northern quarter.

name: Suhotra
description: Vanara warrior enumerated among Sugriva's commanders.

name: Sushena
description: Aged physician of the vanara army and father-in-law of Sugriva, who sent Hanuman for the Sanjivani herb.

name: Vali
description: Mighty son of Indra, elder brother of Sugriva and king of Kishkindha, slain by Rama's arrow.

name: Vinata
description: Vanara commander appointed by Sugriva to lead one of the four search parties (the eastern quarter).

name: Indrajit (Meghanada)
description: Son of Ravana, conqueror of Indra, master of maya and the Brahmastra, slain by Lakshmana in the war.

name: Kumbhakarna
description: Ravana's giant brother cursed to sleep for six months at a stretch; awakened for the war, he fell to Rama's arrows.

name: Mandodari
description: Chief queen of Ravana, daughter of Mayasura. One of the five legendary Panchakanya for her virtue.

name: Ravana
description: Ten-headed king of Lanka, son of Vishrava and Kaikasi, great scholar and devotee of Shiva whose pride brought his fall.

name: Akampana
description: Rakshasa counsellor who advised Ravana to abduct Sita by guile, slain later in the war.

name: Aksha (Akshayakumara)
description: Young son of Ravana slain by Hanuman during the burning of Lanka.

name: Atikaya
description: Son of Ravana and Dhanyamalini, a giant-bodied warrior slain by Lakshmana with a wind-borne arrow.

name: Devantaka
description: Son of Ravana, slain by Hanuman in the siege of Lanka.

name: Dhumraksha
description: Rakshasa general dispatched by Ravana, slain by Hanuman in the siege.

name: Dundubhi
description: Buffalo-shaped asura slain by Vali, whose bones Rama kicked to demonstrate his strength to Sugriva.

name: Dushana
description: Lieutenant of Khara at Janasthana, slain by Rama alongside his commander.

name: Heti
description: Primordial rakshasa ancestor mentioned in the Uttara Kanda genealogy.

name: Kabandha
description: Headless rakshasa cursed to a monstrous form; freed by Rama's cremation, he rose as a gandharva and pointed Rama to Sugriva.

name: Kaikasi
description: Rakshasi mother of Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Vibhishana and Shurpanakha, daughter of Sumali.

name: Khara
description: Cousin of Ravana commanding the rakshasa host at Janasthana, slain by Rama with the whole army of fourteen thousand.

name: Kumbha
description: Son of Kumbhakarna, slain by Sugriva in battle.

name: Lankini
description: Tutelary rakshasi of the city of Lanka whom Hanuman struck down at the gates, fulfilling an old prophecy.

name: Mahakaya
description: Rakshasa warrior of great stature listed in the hosts of Lanka.

name: Mahaparshva
description: Rakshasa warrior of Ravana's inner council, slain by Angada.

name: Mahodara
description: Rakshasa counsellor and warrior of Lanka, slain in battle with Sugriva.

name: Makaraksha
description: Son of Khara who came to avenge his father in the war and fell to Rama's arrow.

name: Mali
description: Rakshasa brother of Sumali and Malyavan, slain by Vishnu in the ancient wars that preceded Ravana's rise.

name: Malyavan
description: Aged maternal uncle of Ravana who counselled peace with Rama and was ignored.

name: Maricha
description: Son of Tataka who assumed the form of the golden deer to lure Rama away so Ravana could abduct Sita.

name: Mayasura
description: Great asura architect and father of Mandodari, builder of magical palaces.

name: Mayavi
description: Son of Dundubhi whose pursuit into a cave estranged Vali from Sugriva and set their tragic quarrel in motion.

name: Narantaka
description: Son of Ravana, slain by Angada in the siege of Lanka.

name: Nikumbha
description: Son of Kumbhakarna, a powerful warrior slain by Hanuman in the war.

name: Prahasta
description: Chief commander of Ravana's armies, slain by Nila on the third day of the great battle.

name: Praheti
description: Brother of Heti in the primordial rakshasa ancestry.

name: Prajangha
description: Rakshasa warrior listed among Ravana's commanders in the great siege.

name: Rashmiketu
description: Rakshasa chief in the army of Lanka, killed in the great war.

name: Sarama
description: Wife of Vibhishana, friend and comforter of Sita in the Ashoka Vatika.

name: Sarana
description: Rakshasa minister and spy of Ravana, paired with Shuka in reconnaissance missions.

name: Shuka
description: Rakshasa minister and messenger of Ravana sent to spy on and parley with Sugriva.

name: Shurpanakha
description: Sister of Ravana whose advances Rama rejected and whose mutilation by Lakshmana ignited the war.

name: Simhika
description: Shadow-seizing sea demoness who caught Hanuman by his shadow as he leapt toward Lanka; slain by him.

name: Subahu (rakshasa)
description: Son of Tataka and brother of Maricha, slain by Rama during Vishwamitra's sacrifice.

name: Sumali
description: Maternal grandfather of Ravana, ancient rakshasa patriarch of Lanka restored after the fall of the Nagas.

name: Sunda
description: Yaksha husband of Tataka, father of Maricha, slain earlier by sage Agastya.

name: Suparshva
description: Rakshasa minister who reminded Ravana of dharma and stopped him from forcing himself on the captive Sita.

name: Suryashatru
description: Rakshasa warrior enumerated among those fallen in the siege of Lanka.

name: Tataka
description: Yakshini cursed into a rakshasi form, terror of the sages, slain by Rama in his very first battle.

name: Trijata
description: Elder rakshasi in the Ashoka Vatika who dreamed of Ravana's doom and comforted the grieving Sita.

name: Trishira (Khara's general)
description: A three-headed rakshasa commander under Khara at Janasthana, slain by Rama.

name: Trishira (son of Ravana)
description: Three-headed son of Ravana, slain in battle. Distinct from Khara's general of the same name.

name: Vajradamshtra
description: Rakshasa commander of Lanka, slain by Angada.

name: Vidyujjihva
description: Master illusionist of Lanka who created the false head of Rama to break Sita's will in the Ashoka Vatika.

name: Viradha
description: Cursed gandharva in rakshasa form who seized Sita in the Dandaka forest and was buried alive by Rama and Lakshmana.

name: Virupaksha
description: Rakshasa chieftain among Ravana's commanders at the great battle.

name: Yajnakopa
description: Rakshasa warrior in Ravana's host, felled during the battle of Lanka.

name: Suketu
description: Yaksha father of Tataka whose tapas won her a son's strength.
